title: Conditional assembly and mapping-space property of free operadic cocones
statement:
Use the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads and inert-preserving algebra functors as defined in [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], without its presentability hypotheses, and operadically colimiting active cocones as defined in [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. Let $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, with both zero-fibres Kan complexes and $u_{[0]}$ an equivalence. Let $\mathcal V$ be any monoidal infinity category; neither cocompleteness nor presentability is assumed. Put $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)=\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{inert}}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ and similarly for $\mathcal N$.

For an $\mathcal M$-algebra $B$ and a colour $n\in\mathcal N_{[1]}$, set
$$K_n=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}}\times_{\mathcal N_{\mathrm{act}}}(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{act}})_{/n},\qquad
T_n:K_n\longrightarrow\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}}\xrightarrow{B}\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}.$$
Pullbacks and slices here retain coherent homotopies; equivalently $K_n$ parametrizes pairs $(m,\alpha:u(m)\to n)$ with $\alpha$ active, and morphisms are active arrows in $\mathcal M$ with their commuting-triangle homotopies. There exist an $\mathcal N$-algebra $A$ and a transformation $\eta:B\to u^*A$ for which the induced cocones $T_n\to A(n)$ are all operadically colimiting if and only if each $T_n$ admits an operadically colimiting extension with apex in $\mathcal V$. Each extension is required to lie over the canonical base cocone: the active arrows $\alpha:u(m)\to n$ and their commuting-triangle homotopies give a coherent transformation from the base of $T_n$ to the constant diagram $[1]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the extension projects to this transformation. For a pair $(A,\eta)$ the induced cocone at $(m,\alpha)$ is $B(m)\xrightarrow{\eta_m}A(u(m))\xrightarrow{A(\alpha)}A(n)$, with $\eta_m$ taken in the fibre containing $m$.

For every such pair $(A,\eta)$ and every $\mathcal N$-algebra $C$, the map
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal V)}(A,C)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)}(B,u^*C),\qquad
h\longmapsto u^*(h)\circ\eta,$$
is an equivalence, natural in $C$, with its higher homotopies. This assertion is conditional on the active cocones and does not assert that they exist in an arbitrary $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Gepner--Haugseng v4, Definition A.4.1, Proposition A.4.4 (conditional existence) and Proposition A.4.3 (mapping-space equivalence) Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] to $u$ and denote its correspondence by $\mathcal P_u$. It is small, constant over $[0]$, and has space zero-fibers by exactly the hypotheses on $u$. For a target color $n$, its source active slice is $\mathcal M\times_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{act}})_{/n}$. This is the $K_n$ in the statement: any source arrow in this pullback has active image in $\mathcal N$, hence active base arrow in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, hence belongs to $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{act}}$, since $u$ lies over the base. The same observation holds on all simplices of these wide active subcategories. The comparison respects the source diagram and the canonical base cocone. The coherent comma description identifies a functor $H:\mathcal P_u\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ preserving fiberwise inert edges with a triple $(B,A,\eta)$, and identifies its cocone at $(m,\alpha)$ with $B(m)\xrightarrow{\eta_m}A(u(m))\xrightarrow{A(\alpha)}A(n)$. Thus, by [def-coef-operadic-correspondence], this $H$ is an operadic left Kan extension exactly when the induced cocones in the statement are operadically colimiting.

source.place: Remark A.4.2 and Definition A.3.3; identify the active slices and their actual cocones.

proof.text: If a pair $(A,\eta)$ as in the statement exists, its induced cocone at each color is itself the required extension of $T_n$. Its projection is the specified canonical base cocone because $\eta$ is over the identity in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $A(\alpha)$ projects to the base of $\alpha$. This proves necessity without any colimit existence assumption.

source.place: Definition A.4.1 and the necessary direction of Proposition A.4.4.

proof.text: Conversely assume the specified operadically colimiting extensions of every $T_n$ exist. By step 1 they supply exactly the local active cocones for $B$ on the source of $\mathcal P_u$. The existence assertion of [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling] therefore gives an inert-preserving $H:\mathcal P_u\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ restricting to $B$, which is an operadic left Kan extension. All its hypotheses were checked in step 1; its target may be any monoidal infinity category. Under [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] this gives $A$ and $\eta$ together. The comparison respects cocones, so their cocones have the required operadic colimit property by [def-coef-operadic-correspondence]. This assembles coherent algebra data rather than choosing operations separately.

source.place: Theorem A.3.4(1), Remark A.4.2, and the sufficient direction of Proposition A.4.4.

proof.text:
For any pair $(A,\eta)$ with the cocone property, put $H=(B,A,\eta)$ in $\mathcal E=\mathcal E_{\mathcal P_u}(\mathcal V)$. It is an operadic left Kan extension by step 1. For any $G\in\mathcal E$ with source restriction $Y$, consider restriction
$$\rho:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)}(B,Y).$$
We verify lifting against every $\partial\Delta^q\hookrightarrow\Delta^q$, including $q=0$. Use the right-pinched definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $q>0$, a map from $\partial\Delta^q$ to the left mapping space specifies all proper faces of $\Delta^{q+1}$ containing its final vertex. Adjoin the entire initial face $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,q\}}$ as the constant simplex $H$. For $q=0$ the mapping-space boundary is empty, so instead prescribe both vertices of $\Delta^1$ directly: vertex $0$ is $H$ and vertex $1$ is the fixed target $G$. In either case these data specify the whole boundary $\partial\Delta^{q+1}$, with the final vertex fixed at $G$. The proposed simplex on the right supplies the compatible source diagram on $\mathcal M\times\Delta^{q+1}$ with that initial face constant at $B$. These are precisely the prescribed data of the relative boundary assertion in [lem-coef-operadic-correspondence-kan-filling], with $m=q+1>0$. Its initial vertex is $H$, an operadic left Kan extension. A filler preserves the initial face and final vertex and hence is the required right-pinched simplex. For $q=0$, it fills the edge with prescribed vertices $H,G$, so surjectivity on vertices is included. The collage comparison guarantees that $\mathcal E$ and its endpoint algebra categories are quasicategories. By [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], lifting every boundary makes $\rho$ a trivial Kan fibration, therefore a weak homotopy equivalence. This proves universality on mapping spaces, not just on their components.

source.place: Proposition A.4.3 via the relative boundary consequence of Theorem A.3.4; explicit mapping-simplex calculation.

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal N$-algebra $C$, take $G_C=(u^*C,C,\operatorname{id})$. The natural mapping formula of [lem-coef-operadic-collage-comparison] gives, writing $D=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)}(B,u^*C)$ and $F=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal N}(\mathcal V)}(A,C)$,
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(H,G_C)\simeq D\times_D^h F,$$
where the first leg is the identity and the second is $h\mapsto u^*(h)\circ\eta$. Projection to $F$ is an equivalence: its fiber over $h$ is the space of paths with arbitrary initial point and fixed endpoint $u^*(h)\eta$, contracted by moving the initial point along the path toward that endpoint. Its inverse chooses the constant path. Under this equivalence $\rho$ is the displayed map $F\to D$, with its specified coherent composition homotopy. Step 4 proves that map is an equivalence. The comma formula is natural in all morphism parameters, and restriction and composition define coherent transformations. Consequently the displayed map is natural in $C$ on its whole infinity category, retaining all higher homotopies.
